hypotheses: finite real set in general position
main_written_result.conclusion: A four-cap-free subset containing the root meets every convex (n-1)-gon; a terminal-safe deletion solution exists in the corresponding direction.

additional_written_results: A terminal-rank-three cap a<b<c forces beta(a)<beta(b).
Every single beta-level is terminal-safe in a five-cap-free set.
If U has no (n-2)-cup, the right endpoints of its (n-1)-gons give a terminal-safe weak Delta, at any size.
For an arbitrary root, cardinality at most 2*n-4 suffices without no-n-gon.
At cardinality 2*n-2, failure of terminal-safe deletion selection forces maximum old cup length n-2 and a convex (n-1)-gon complement to every maximum cup.
parent_lemma_review: Arbitrary-root n+3 under no-five-cap and no-n-gon is sound; attributed to parent.
projective_sign_correction: For T(x,y)=(x/(1-x),y/(1-x)) and root (1,0), cap extension is POSITIVE transformed last slope. Old four-caps have negative last slope in a five-cap-free full set.
illustrative_refutation: Seven real points with no five-cap or convex six-gon have no five-point four-cap-free subset containing their rightmost point. All 15 failures checked; not a Delta counterexample.
controls: Independent exact integer/fraction checker PASS; no solver or certification claims.
open: General favorable terminal-safe or minimum-envelope selection
